copy.name: How to find the best bedtime
copy.blurb: Count back from your alarm in 90-minute cycles plus 14 minutes to fall asleep. A 07:00 alarm means bed at 23:16 for five cycles or 21:46 for six.
copy.title: How to find the best bedtime
copy.lead: You have an alarm time. You will find the bedtimes that end a whole sleep cycle, so the alarm rings in light sleep instead of deep sleep. A cycle is about 90 minutes and falling asleep takes about 14 minutes. For a 07:00 alarm, five cycles means lights out at 23:16.
copy.result: A short list of bedtimes for six, five, four and three cycles, or wake-up times if you start from your bedtime.
copy.note: Open the sleep calculator when you know your alarm time. Pick five or six cycles on a normal night. The shorter options are for nights when you must. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s1b: One cycle is about 90 minutes: light sleep, deep sleep, then REM. Falling asleep takes about 14 minutes. Waking at the end of a cycle feels lighter than waking in the middle of one.
copy.s2b: Wake-up time is selected and 07:00 is filled. The bedtimes sit on the right. Nothing leaves this tab.
copy.s3b: Type the time the alarm rings, for example 06:30. Four bedtimes appear: six cycles (9 hours), five (7.5), four (6) and three (4.5). The two longest are marked.
copy.s4b: For 07:00, six cycles is 21:46 and five is 23:16. Most adults do well on 7.5 to 9 hours. 00:46 (four cycles) and 02:16 (three) are for short nights, not every night.
copy.s5b: Switch I know my to Bedtime and enter when you lie down, for example 23:00. The list flips to wake-up times: 03:44, 05:14, 06:44 and 08:14. Set the alarm on one of them.
copy.s6b: If you usually fall asleep in five minutes, go to bed nine minutes later than the list says. If you wake groggy at the suggested time, try the next cycle up or down for a week. Copy puts the list on the clipboard.
copy.diagram1: Six to three cycles of 90 minutes count back from a 07:00 alarm, each plus 14 minutes to fall asleep.
copy.diagram2: A 23:00 bedtime plus 14 minutes gives wake-up times at 03:44, 05:14, 06:44 and 08:14.

faq.q1: Can I find a bedtime free online?
faq.a1: Yes. cv.cm counts the cycles in this tab. Nothing is uploaded or stored.
faq.a2: Five cycles of 90 minutes is 450 minutes, plus 14 minutes to fall asleep, counted back from 07:00.
faq.q3: How many hours should I sleep?
faq.a3: Five or six cycles, 7.5 to 9 hours, suit most adults. Three or four cycles are shown for nights when you have no choice.
faq.a4: No. Cycles range from about 70 to 120 minutes and change through the night. Treat the times as a starting point and adjust by how you feel.
faq.a5: No. It only lists times. Set the alarm on your phone or clock.

copy.name: How to measure body fat with a tape
copy.blurb: Measure neck, waist and hips, enter them with your height, and read the U.S. Navy body fat percentage and its category. Add weight to see fat and lean mass.
copy.title: How to measure body fat with a tape
copy.lead: You have a tape measure. You will take three or four measurements in centimetres and turn them into a body fat percentage with the U.S. Navy formula. A man of 175 cm with a 38 cm neck and 85 cm waist is about 17%. Nothing leaves this tab.
copy.result: A body fat percentage, an ACE category such as fitness or average, and fat and lean mass if you entered weight.
copy.note: Open the body fat calculator after measuring. Measure in the morning before eating, with the tape snug but not tight. Repeat the same way to compare over time. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s1b: Neck: just below the larynx, tape sloping slightly down to the front. Waist: at the navel for men, at the narrowest point for women. Hips (women): at the widest point. Read the tape in centimetres, snug but not pressing in.
copy.s2t: Open Body fat calculator on cv.cm
copy.s2b: Metric and male are selected with sample numbers. The percentage sits on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s3b: Type your height, neck and waist in centimetres. Switch to imperial for inches. For a woman, pick Female and the hips field appears; the formula needs it.
copy.s4t: Add weight if you want mass
copy.s4b: Weight is optional. With 70 kg and 17%, fat mass is 11.9 kg and lean mass 58.1 kg. Leave it blank to see only the percentage.
copy.s5b: ACE ranges for men: essential 2–5%, athletes 6–13%, fitness 14–17%, average 18–24%, obese 25%+. For women: 10–13%, 14–20%, 21–24%, 25–31%, 32%+.
copy.s6t: Compare over time, not with a scan
copy.s6b: The tape method is usually within 3 to 4 points of a DEXA scan and less accurate for very lean or very muscular people. Measure the same way every few weeks and watch the trend. Copy puts the result on the clipboard.
copy.diagram1: Tape positions: neck below the larynx, waist at the navel (men) or narrowest point (women), hips at the widest point.
copy.diagram2: 175 cm, 38 cm neck, 85 cm waist: about 17%, in the fitness band for men.

faq.q1: Can I estimate body fat free online?
faq.a1: Yes. cv.cm runs the U.S. Navy formula in this tab. Nothing is uploaded or stored.
faq.a2: Height, neck and waist for men; height, neck, waist and hips for women. Weight is optional and only splits fat and lean mass.
faq.a3: At the navel for men and at the narrowest point for women, tape level and snug.
faq.q4: How accurate is the tape method?
faq.a4: Within about 3 to 4 percentage points of a DEXA scan for most adults. It is better for tracking change than for one exact number.
faq.q5: What is a healthy body fat?
faq.a5: By the ACE ranges, fitness is 14–17% for men and 21–24% for women, and average is 18–24% and 25–31%. Ask a doctor about your own case.

copy.name: How to check color contrast for WCAG
copy.blurb: Enter the text and background hex colors and read the ratio. Normal text needs 4.5:1 for AA and 7:1 for AAA; large text needs 3:1 and 4.5:1. A passing color is suggested.
copy.title: How to check color contrast for WCAG
copy.lead: You have a text color and a background color. You will read their contrast ratio and see whether the pair passes WCAG 2 AA and AAA. Grey #777777 on white is 4.48:1 and fails AA for normal text by a hair; #767676 passes. Nothing leaves this tab.
copy.result: A ratio such as 4.48:1, pass or fail for AA and AAA at normal and large sizes, and the closest text color that passes when the pair fails.
copy.note: Open the contrast checker with both hex codes at hand. Check body text against 4.5:1, headings over 24px against 3:1, and icons or borders against 3:1. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s1b: WCAG 2 AA: 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. AAA: 7:1 and 4.5:1. Large text is 24px regular or about 18.7px bold. Icons, borders and form controls need 3:1.
copy.s2b: A sample pink on cream pair is filled. The ratio and the pass/fail rows sit on the right under a text sample. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s3b: Type a hex code such as #777777 for text and #ffffff for background, or pick with the color swatch. Three-digit codes like #777 work too. The sample updates as you type.
copy.s4t: Read the ratio and the rows
copy.s4b: #777777 on #ffffff is 4.48:1: AA large text and UI pass, AA normal text fails. Each row says Pass or Fail against its threshold.
copy.s5b: When normal text fails AA, the page suggests the closest text color that reaches 4.5:1, moving toward black or white. For #777777 on white it suggests #767676. Swap exchanges text and background.
copy.s6b: Repeat for links, hover and disabled colors, and for text on images use the darkest part of the image as background. Copy puts the colors, ratio and results on the clipboard.
copy.diagram1: Ratio thresholds: 3:1 for large text and UI, 4.5:1 for AA normal text, 7:1 for AAA normal text.
copy.diagram2: #777777 on white is 4.48:1 and fails AA normal text; #767676 reaches 4.54:1 and passes.

faq.q1: Can I check color contrast free online?
faq.a1: Yes. cv.cm computes the WCAG ratio in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
faq.q2: What ratio does normal text need?
faq.a2: 4.5:1 for AA and 7:1 for AAA. Large text needs 3:1 and 4.5:1.
faq.q4: Does the order of the colors matter?
faq.a4: No. The ratio is the same either way. Swap only changes the preview.
faq.a5: Its ratio on white is 4.48:1, just under 4.5:1. #767676 reaches 4.54:1 and passes.

copy.name: How to calculate running pace
copy.blurb: Enter distance and time to get pace per km and per mile, or enter pace to get a finish time. 10 km in 55:00 is 5:30 /km, 8:51 /mi, and a 3:52:04 marathon at the same pace.
copy.title: How to calculate running pace
copy.lead: You ran a distance in a time, or you want to finish in a time. You will turn that into pace per kilometre and per mile, and see what the same pace gives for 5K, 10K, half and marathon. 10 km in 55:00 is 5:30 /km. Nothing leaves this tab.
copy.result: Pace per km and per mile, speed, and finish times for the four common races at the same pace.
copy.note: Open the pace calculator with the numbers from your watch or race plan. Type time as h:mm:ss or mm:ss and pace as m:ss. Race predictions assume an even pace. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s1t: Pick what you want to find
copy.s1b: Pace = time ÷ distance. Time = pace × distance. Distance = time ÷ pace. Decide which one you are missing; you fill in the other two.
copy.s2b: Pace is selected with 10 km in 55:00. The result and race times sit on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s3b: Type 10 for distance and 55:00 for time. The pace reads 05:30 per km and 08:51 per mile, and the speed 10.91 km/h. Switch Unit to mi for miles.
copy.s4t: Or enter pace to get a time
copy.s4b: Set Calculate to Time, type the distance and a pace such as 5:00. A half marathon at 5:00 /km finishes in 1:45:29.
copy.s5b: At 5:30 /km: 5K 27:30, 10K 55:00, half 1:56:02, marathon 3:52:04. Real races slow over distance, so plan a longer race a little slower than a short one.
copy.s6b: Copy puts distance, time, both paces, speed and the four race times on the clipboard for a training log.
copy.diagram1: Pace = time ÷ distance: 55:00 over 10 km is 5:30 per km or 8:51 per mile.

faq.q1: Can I calculate running pace free online?
faq.a1: Yes. cv.cm does the math in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
faq.q2: What is 10 km in 55 minutes as pace?
faq.a2: 5:30 per km, 8:51 per mile, or 10.91 km/h.
faq.q3: How do I convert pace per km to per mile?
faq.a3: Multiply by 1.609. The page shows both at once.
faq.a4: They assume you hold the same pace. Most runners slow a little over longer distances, so treat them as a best case.
faq.a5: h:mm:ss or mm:ss, such as 1:45:29 or 55:00. Pace takes m:ss, such as 5:30.

copy.name: How to calculate the grade you need on a final
copy.blurb: Enter your current grade, the grade you want and the final's weight. 85% now, 90% wanted and a 30% final needs 101.7%, so aim for a B instead. Needed = (wanted − current × (1 − weight)) ÷ weight.
copy.title: How to calculate the grade you need on a final
copy.lead: You know your grade so far, the grade you want and how much the final counts. You will find the score the final must reach. With 85% now, a 90% goal and a 30% final, you need 101.7%, which means an A is out of reach but a B needs only 68.3%. Nothing leaves this tab.
copy.result: The score needed on the final, a note when it is over 100% or already reached, and a table for A, B, C and D.
copy.note: Open the final grade calculator with the syllabus at hand for the final's weight. Use your current weighted average as the current grade. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s1b: Current grade: your average so far, as a percentage. Grade you want: the target for the course. Weight of the final: from the syllabus, such as 30%. The rest of the course is then 70%.
copy.s2t: Open Final grade calculator on cv.cm
copy.s2b: 85%, 90% and a 30% final are filled. The needed score sits on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s3b: Type the current grade, the wanted grade and the weight. The needed score updates as you type: with 85, 90 and 30 it reads 101.7% on the final.
copy.s4b: Over 100% means the goal cannot be reached on the final alone without extra credit. Look at the letter table: a B (80%) needs 68.3%, a C needs 35%.
copy.s5t: Read a result at 0% or below
copy.s5b: With 95% now, 90% wanted and a 20% final, the needed score is 70%. If the result is 0% or less, you already have the grade and any score keeps it.
copy.s6b: Needed = (wanted − current × (1 − weight)) ÷ weight. For 90, 85 and 0.30: (90 − 59.5) ÷ 0.30 = 101.7. Copy puts the result and the table on the clipboard.
copy.diagram1: Needed = (wanted − current × (1 − weight)) ÷ weight. 85% now, 90% wanted, 30% final: 101.7%.
copy.diagram2: Same numbers per letter: A needs 101.7%, B 68.3%, C 35%, D 1.7%.

faq.q1: Can I find the grade I need on a final free online?
faq.a1: Yes. cv.cm does the math in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
faq.a2: Needed = (wanted − current × (1 − weight)) ÷ weight, with the weight as a fraction such as 0.30.
faq.q3: What if I need more than 100%?
faq.a3: The target is out of reach on the final alone. Check the table for the highest letter you can still get.
faq.a4: Your weighted average on everything graded before the final, as your gradebook shows it.
faq.q5: Does the weight of the final matter a lot?
faq.a5: Yes. With 85% now and 90% wanted, a 30% final needs 101.7% but a 50% final needs only 95%.

copy.name: How to calculate TDEE and daily calories
copy.blurb: Enter sex, age, weight, height and activity. BMR comes from Mifflin–St Jeor and TDEE is BMR times an activity factor. A 30-year-old man, 70 kg, 175 cm, moderate activity: 1649 and 2556 kcal.
copy.title: How to calculate TDEE and daily calories
copy.lead: You want to know how many calories you burn in a day. You will enter five numbers and read BMR (at rest) and TDEE (with activity), plus a cut and a bulk target. A 30-year-old man of 70 kg and 175 cm with moderate activity burns about 2556 kcal a day. Nothing leaves this tab.
copy.result: BMR, TDEE, a weight-loss target 500 kcal below and a gain target 300 kcal above, with a floor for safe cutting.
copy.note: Open the TDEE calculator with your weight and height at hand. Pick the activity level honestly; most desk workers who train three times a week are light or moderate. An estimate, not medical advice. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s1b: BMR is the energy you burn at complete rest. TDEE multiplies it by an activity factor from 1.2 (sedentary) to 1.9 (training twice a day). Eat at TDEE to hold weight.
copy.s2b: Metric, male, 30 years, 70 kg, 175 cm and moderate are filled. The calories sit on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s3b: Pick sex, type age, weight and height. Switch to imperial for pounds, feet and inches; the numbers convert as you switch. Age 15 to 100 is accepted.
copy.s4b: Sedentary 1.2: desk job, little exercise. Light 1.375: 1–3 days a week. Moderate 1.55: 3–5 days. Active 1.725: hard exercise 6–7 days. Very active 1.9: physical job or two sessions a day.
copy.s5b: For the sample man: BMR 1649, maintain 2556, lose 2056 (−500 kcal, about 0.5 kg a week), gain 2856 (+300 kcal). The cut never goes below 1500 kcal for men or 1200 for women; a note says when it was raised.
copy.s6b: Weigh yourself weekly. If weight does not move at the cut target after four weeks, choose the next lower activity level and recalculate. Copy puts the four numbers on the clipboard.
copy.diagram1: BMR from Mifflin–St Jeor, TDEE = BMR × activity factor 1.2 to 1.9.
copy.diagram2: Sample man: maintain 2556, lose 2056 (−500), gain 2856 (+300) kcal a day.

faq.q1: Can I calculate TDEE free online?
faq.a1: Yes. cv.cm computes it in this tab. Nothing is uploaded or stored.
faq.a2: Mifflin–St Jeor for BMR: 10 × kg + 6.25 × cm − 5 × age, plus 5 for men or minus 161 for women. TDEE is BMR × activity factor.
faq.q3: How much should I cut to lose weight?
faq.a3: The page subtracts 500 kcal, about 0.5 kg a week, but never below 1500 kcal for men or 1200 for women.
faq.a4: Most desk workers who exercise 1–3 times a week are light; 3–5 times is moderate. When unsure, pick the lower one.
faq.a5: No. It is an estimate for healthy adults. Ask a doctor or dietitian before a big change.

copy.name: How to calculate GPA on the 4.0 scale
copy.blurb: Enter a letter grade and credits per course. Each grade becomes points (A 4.0, B+ 3.3, B 3.0), points times credits are added and divided by total credits. A 3, B+ 3, A- 4, B 3 gives 3.51.
copy.title: How to calculate GPA on the 4.0 scale
copy.lead: You have letter grades and credits for the term. You will turn them into a credit-weighted GPA on the 4.0 scale. Four courses, A (3 credits), B+ (3), A- (4) and B (3), give 45.7 points over 13 credits, a GPA of 3.51. Nothing leaves this tab.
copy.result: A GPA to two decimals, total credits, quality points and the number of courses counted.
copy.note: Open the GPA calculator with your transcript at hand. Pass/fail courses do not count. If your school gives A+ 4.3, tick the box. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s2b: Four sample courses are filled. GPA, credits and quality points sit on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s3b: Pick the letter grade and type the credits in each row. Add course adds a row; × removes one. Credits above 30 or 0 are skipped as typos.
copy.s4b: A × 3 = 12, B+ × 3 = 9.9, A- × 4 = 14.8, B × 3 = 9. Total 45.7 points over 13 credits = 3.51. Quality points and total credits are shown so you can check.
copy.s5b: Tick A+ = 4.3 only if your school uses it; the GPA can then exceed 4.0. Leave pass/fail courses out; they usually add credits but no points.
copy.s6b: Copy puts the GPA, total credits, quality points and course count on the clipboard. For a cumulative GPA, add every term's courses in one list.
copy.diagram1: Letter to points: A 4.0, A- 3.7, B+ 3.3, B 3.0, C 2.0, D 1.0, F 0.
copy.diagram2: A 3, B+ 3, A- 4, B 3: 45.7 points over 13 credits = 3.51.

faq.q1: Can I calculate GPA free online?
faq.a1: Yes. cv.cm does the math in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
faq.a2: Each grade becomes points, multiplied by the course credits. The sum of points is divided by the sum of credits.
faq.a3: By default A+ is 4.0. Tick A+ = 4.3 if your school uses that scale.
faq.a4: Usually not. Leave them out of the list.
faq.q5: How do I get a cumulative GPA?
faq.a5: Put every course from every term in one list. The result is weighted by credits across all of them.

copy.name: How to use a Pomodoro timer
copy.blurb: Start a 25-minute focus block, rest 5 minutes at the chime, and take a 15-minute break after four rounds. The tab title shows the time left; the chime needs the tab open.
copy.title: How to use a Pomodoro timer
copy.lead: You have a task that keeps slipping. You will work in 25-minute blocks with 5-minute breaks and a 15-minute break after four. The timer counts from the clock, chimes at each change and moves to the next phase by itself. Nothing leaves this tab.
copy.result: A running countdown in the page and the tab title, a chime at each change, and a count of finished focus blocks.
copy.note: Open the Pomodoro timer before you start the task, not during it. Write one task per block. Keep the tab open for the chime. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s1b: Write down the one thing for the next 25 minutes. Close chat and mail. A block that gets interrupted does not count; start it again.
copy.s2b: 25-minute focus, 5-minute short break, 15-minute long break and 4 rounds are set. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s3b: The clock counts down and the tab title shows the time left, so you can switch tabs. At 00:00 a chime plays and the break starts by itself.
copy.s4b: Stand up, drink water, do not open the task. After the 5-minute break the next focus block starts on its own. After four blocks the break is 15 minutes.
copy.s5b: Pause stops the clock without losing time. Skip jumps to the next phase; a skipped focus block does not count toward the long break. Reset starts over from round 1.
copy.s6b: While stopped, set focus, short break and long break from 1 to 180 minutes and rounds from 1 to 12. 50/10 suits deep work; 15/3 suits chores. The current phase takes the new length right away.
copy.diagram1: Four 25-minute focus blocks with 5-minute breaks, then a 15-minute long break.
copy.diagram2: Pause keeps the time left; Skip moves on without counting the block; Reset starts at round 1.

faq.q1: Can I use a Pomodoro timer free online?
faq.a1: Yes. cv.cm runs it in this tab. Nothing is sent or stored.
faq.a2: Work for 25 minutes, rest 5, and take a 15-minute break after four blocks. Each block is one pomodoro.
faq.q3: Will it chime in a background tab?
faq.a3: Yes, while the tab stays open. The timer follows the clock and the tab title shows the time left.
faq.a4: Yes, from 1 to 180 minutes for each phase and 1 to 12 rounds, while the clock is stopped.
faq.a5: No. Only finished focus blocks count toward the long break.
